title: TIC annual survey — preliminary Report on Foreign Portfolio Holdings of U.S. Securities at end-June 2026, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes) by the tic-monthly-2027-01-19 initial-research adjacency sweep — its 2027 table's February row reads '26 - prelim.' in the column headed 'Annual: Foreign portfolio holdings of U.S. securities at end-June of previous year', under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. The same page's notes state 'Preliminary data for the survey are released on the last business day of February; the final report is released on the last business day of April' and, separately, 'The time of release is normally at 04:00 p.m. in Washington D.C.' Corroborated mechanically and exactly: 2027-02-28 is a Sunday and 2027-02-27 a Saturday, so the last business day of February 2027 is 2027-02-26, offset +0 from the page's own stated rule. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, and because this is a distinct series from the monthly release the proposer owns. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-monthly-2027-01-19 initial research (2026-09-09). THIS OVERTURNS A PRIOR DECLINE, ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN PREFERENCE, and the reason is the whole point of proposing it. Three sibling ledgers (tic-monthly-2026-09-16, -10-16 and -12-15) each met the annual survey's October counterpart in their own sweeps and each declined it on the same ground: 'a different series on a yearly cadence'. This session measured something none of them had. Diffing 29 archived TIC press-notice PDF vintages cell by cell (2024-01 through 2026-08), the LARGEST restatements in the entire panel are not the Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct revision editions Treasury's note (c) advertises — they are the February and March vintages, which moved a CLOSED calendar-year total by up to $745.9bn (2024-02, line 30) and $127.9bn (2025-03), against a maximum of $54.8bn for any revision edition and a median of $5.0bn for an ordinary one. February/March is exactly when the preliminary annual survey's benchmark feeds back into the monthly series (with footnote 9's series break sitting in the same window). So the survey is not a parallel series that happens to share a website: it is the single largest input to the revisions of the monthly series this calendar already tracks, and the monthly ledgers have been reading vintage changes without it on the board. Excluding those vintages is what turns the revision-edition test from a flat null (p=0.78) into a real effect ($5.01bn vs $1.67bn, t=+3.93) — the exclusion is a judgment this session made after seeing the data, and putting the survey on the calendar is how the next sweep gets to check it rather than inherit it. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is eight months stale at publication, no house playbook is macro-keyed) — the value is as the dated cause of a revision, not as a tradeable print. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
